### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4de4e3e997e019fcafa32e0010ebd8266d6650e0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4e1b82182fd7f07e56526e1f2a41faa3b1de7067` — the merge of head `bded79bb60a11e0adfb7c322c3806962d5cb8915` into base `4de4e3e997e019fcafa32e0010ebd8266d6650e0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4e1b82182fd7f07e56526e1f2a41faa3b1de7067 && git checkout 4e1b82182fd7f07e56526e1f2a41faa3b1de7067
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4de4e3e997e019fcafa32e0010ebd8266d6650e0 bded79bb60a11e0adfb7c322c3806962d5cb8915 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4de4e3e997e019fcafa32e0010ebd8266d6650e0 && git merge --no-ff bded79bb60a11e0adfb7c322c3806962d5cb8915

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4de4e3e997e019fcafa32e0010ebd8266d6650e0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bded79bb60a11e0adfb7c322c3806962d5cb8915`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.test.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/comments.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/approvals.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/webhooks.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/auth.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domain-handler-registry.ts` + `.changeset/dispatcher-door-request-kernel-only.md`
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Face: no published schema and no governed path; the review is owed because this is a security fix PR (lane charter `lanes/security.md`), so the scope is every non-prose path of the diff, and the changeset is read for ② only. Rule reviewed against: a dispatcher door bridge reads its door member from the request's own kernel only; a request kernel without the slot answers the door's typed `501`; one reader, built on the existing `getRequestKernelService`; door bridges of the same class folded in; single-kernel and shared-kernel hosts unchanged. Read outside the diff, never reviewed: `http-dispatcher.ts` (`requestKernel`, the deps wiring, the shared resolver), `packages/core` (`kernel.ts`, `plugin-loader.ts`, `lite-kernel.ts`), the slot ledger in `packages/spec/src/contracts/core-service-contracts.ts`, and the plugins registering the six slots the switched reads address.

Gates on this head: 57 check-runs, all completed, 39 `success`, 18 `skipped`, none failed, none running. Among the green ones: `Test Core` and its 10 shards, `TypeScript Type Check` and the four `Type Check` families, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`.

Prior round, judged on the tree: S1 closed (the net finds door modules by scanning and its jsdoc names its markers and its exclusion; see ③b), S2 closed (③c), N2 closed (the qualified-hook branch reads the `automation` engine through `readDoorSlot`, with two behavioural cases on it), N3 closed (the `getRequestKernelService` jsdoc now tells a door to read through `readDoorSlot` and never to add a fall-back, and keeps the share-links engine read as the one named use elsewhere, which matches `share-links.ts`). N1 is carried as a nit.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: none. `readDoorSlot` is exported from `domains/own-door-bridge.ts` only. The package `exports` map addresses `.` and `./compiled-plugin-manifest-file`; `src/index.ts` re-exports nothing from that module. `DomainHandlerDeps` is an exported type and changes in jsdoc only. Right.
- Accept-set: none. No route, status, error code, config key or catalog key is added or removed. The `501` branch of every switched door is outside the diff and still answers through `catalogNotImplemented` with the door's own catalog key. Right.
- A host with one kernel, and any request whose kernel IS the host kernel: no door's answer changes. The reader takes no environment id, so it cannot vary by one; it asks the kernel's `getServiceAsync(name)`, or `getService(name)` on a kernel without it. On both kernels the tree ships (`ObjectKernel`, `LiteKernel`) those accessors read the same registry as every leg the previous readers walked on that kernel (`registerService` and `replaceService` write both maps), and each of the six slots the switched reads address is a plain `ctx.registerService` instance in its plugin (`comments` in `plugin-audit`, `approvals` in `plugin-approvals`, `webhooks` in `plugin-webhooks`, `trigger-api` in its trigger package, `automation` in `service-automation`, `auth` in `plugin-auth`). The three shared-bridge doors reach the same facility they read before the diff. Right.
- A host that places a request on a kernel of its own: a switched door whose slot that kernel lacks answers its `501`. This is the one intended change and the PR body says so. Right.
- `auth.ts`: no answer changes on any host. Its switch is reader uniformity; the type it reads is `IAuthService` before and after. The net is its only pin that turns red on a revert, and the PR's own count for that leg agrees. Right.
- Typing: `comments`, `webhooks` and `trigger-api` now read as their full ledger contract in place of a one-member `Pick` cast. Stricter at compile time only; `TypeScript Type Check` is green. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime: patch` is right: a fix in a released package, no export added, no accept-set moved. `Clause-②: no` is right and needs no arm: nothing a consumer can import or write changes, and the door header in `own-door-bridge.ts` already stated the `501` for a request kernel without the member, so the change makes a stated answer hold; it does not narrow a declared one. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. Both lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; the changeset body stays at rule level; `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) A lookup that throws reads as an empty slot. No outage is newly masked: the three shared-bridge doors carried this same catch before the diff, and the previous readers of the six switched reads absorbed a throwing lookup at every leg and ended at the same empty answer. The catch is unconditional while its sentence names the unregistered-name throw only: N1.
- (b) The completeness net. A door module is any non-test `.ts` under `src/domains/`, at any depth, whose text contains `context.request as Request` or a call to `createOwnDoorBridgeDomain` or `handleOwnDoorBridgeRequest`. Nine modules match on this head, exactly the nine on the pin's floor. Such a module may not spell a call to `deps.resolveService`, `deps.resolveServiceOrLoud`, `deps.getService`, or `deps.getObjectQL` with a second argument; one that hands the request on must contain a `readDoorSlot` call; and the reader's body may name `deps.getRequestKernelService` and nothing else. Can a door bridge escape it? Yes, in the two ways the pin itself names (a module that hands on the request under another spelling or builds its own, and anything outside `src/domains/`) and in one it does not: a refused reader reached other than by the literal `deps.` spelling. The jsdoc now claims what the net holds, with that one hair left over: N2. A false red (a refused spelling in a comment) fails safe, and the PR body says so.
- (c) Overloads. `readDoorSlot` carries the same pair as `getRequestKernelService`: the generic one keyed on `keyof ServiceSlotContracts` answering the slot's contract or `undefined`, and the `string` one answering `any`. The `approvals` cast is justified: `approvals` has no entry in `ServiceSlotContracts`, so the read takes the untyped overload and the `Pick` of `IApprovalService` is the only typing available without a ledger change, which belongs to another PR. The `automation` cast to the local engine slice predates the diff and addresses members beside the contract.
- (d) Reads through the shared resolver outside door bridges are not required by the rule, confirmed: the rule's class is a bridge that forwards the request to a slot member that owns the door, and every remaining such read under `src/domains/` belongs to a handler that owns its door and calls typed members, or to the one module that hands a request it builds itself to a runtime served from a per-request accessor the dispatcher assembles. That module sits outside the net by the pin's own exclusion. The list, by file and line, goes to the security seat in the private note for its own ruling; nothing in it is graded here.
- Named, not graded: a door slot registered with the scoped lifecycle is not readable by this reader, by the reader's stated contract; the tree holds no such registration for any slot. And a request the host's resolver places on no kernel is served from the host kernel, as before: that is the dispatcher's placement, outside the diff.
- SQL push-down (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5): n/a. No query, no id materialisation, no in-app join in the diff.
- "Startup registry reads": the reader looks the slot up on every request and records nothing. Holds.

### ④ Design judgment

The change holds against the rule and the code it cites. `readDoorSlot` wraps `deps.getRequestKernelService` and nothing else; that facility reads `requestKernel(context)` and has no leg onto another kernel. All five door members and the qualified hook's engine read through it; the three shared-bridge doors reach it through the shared body. No second pattern is invented.

Attempts to break it, by reading:

- A slot registered as a scoped factory: the lookup throws, reads as empty, the door answers `501`. No tree plugin registers a door slot that way, so no shipped host changes; see ③.
- A request kernel equal to the host kernel: the reader reads that kernel; unchanged.
- A kernel with only `getService`: the facility falls to it; a synchronous throw inside the async facility is a rejection the reader's `try` absorbs. Unchanged from the previous readers on that kernel.
- `null` versus `undefined`: the reader folds `null` into `undefined`, which keeps the typed overload's return honest; every caller tests falsiness first, then the member's type.
- The localized `501`: each switched door's empty-slot and missing-member branches are untouched and still go through `catalogNotImplemented` with the request's `Accept-Language`; the 16 not-available cases assert status and code on all eight doors through the real `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()`.
- The pins. The harness places the request on its own kernel and also names its environment, so the not-available cases are not vacuous for the four switched bridges: each asserts the door's `501` and that a member held elsewhere is never called, in both the throwing and the answers-nothing variant. The eight preservation cases assert the request kernel's own member serves. The engine has its own two cases. For the auth door the behavioural cases are preservation by construction and the net is the pin, as ① says. The reader is pinned by its own body scan, so a second lookup added inside it turns the net red. `Test Core` is green on this head.

Findings:

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — `readDoorSlot`'s catch absorbs every throw, while its jsdoc sentence names only "a kernel that throws for an unregistered name". Carried from the prior round and unchanged in effect on every door. Telling "never registered" from "registered and failed" is a shared-resolver question, left to the lane.

N2 (nit) — the jsdoc's "holds, exactly" is exact up to spelling: the net refuses the four readers as literal `deps.` calls, and "each such module that reads a slot reads it through this" is held as "contains a `readDoorSlot` call". A refused reader reached through a destructured or optionally-chained `deps`, or a direct `deps.getRequestKernelService` beside the `readDoorSlot` call (still the request's kernel, so the rule holds), passes. Saying "spelled as a `deps.` call" would close the gap in words. A default-deny pin (every module under `src/domains/` that passes an environment id to the shared resolver is on a named list) would close it in fact; that is a follow-up, not owed by this PR.

**VERDICT: PASS**
